Name: PostgreSQL
Strengths: ACID, mature, JSONB, rich extensions (pgvector, PostGIS, TimescaleDB), excellent SQL
Weaknesses: Manual scale-out, vacuum tuning, write scaling without Citus
Cloud Managed Options: AWS RDS/Aurora, Cloud SQL, Azure DB for Postgres, Neon, Supabase
Keywords: postgres postgresql relational jsonb pgvector acid
Notes: Default choice for OLTP. Aurora gives storage-decoupled scale; Citus for HTAP/sharding.

Name: MySQL / MariaDB
Use Case: OLTP, web apps, large social-style read traffic
Strengths: Battle-tested at huge scale (FB/YouTube/Shopify), excellent replication tooling
Weaknesses: Weaker SQL than Postgres, JSON support behind
Cloud Managed Options: AWS RDS/Aurora MySQL, Cloud SQL, Azure DB
Keywords: mysql mariadb vitess innodb async replication
Notes: Vitess is the go-to for sharded MySQL at internet scale.

Name: CockroachDB
Strengths: Postgres-compatible, survives node/AZ/region loss, online schema changes
Weaknesses: Higher write latency vs single-node, expensive cross-region txns
Typical Latency: ms in-region, tens of ms cross-region
Keywords: cockroachdb crdb distributed sql raft multi-region
Notes: Pin tables to regions ('REGIONAL BY ROW') to control latency.

Name: Spanner / TiDB
Keywords: spanner tidb truetime distributed sql htap
Notes: Spanner uses TrueTime; TiDB pairs TiKV (OLTP) + TiFlash (OLAP).

Name: MongoDB
Strengths: Flexible schema, scale-out via sharding, change streams
Weaknesses: Joins/transactions weaker than RDBMS, schema drift risk, costly large docs
Keywords: mongo mongodb document bson sharding replica set
Notes: Use Atlas Search (Lucene) for built-in search; design schema embed-vs-reference deliberately.

Name: Cassandra / ScyllaDB
Strengths: Linear scale, masterless, multi-DC active/active, predictable writes
Weaknesses: Joins/transactions absent, query patterns must drive schema, eventual consistency by default
Keywords: cassandra scylla cql lsm wide column multi-dc
Notes: ScyllaDB = C* protocol-compatible, C++/seastar, much higher per-node throughput.

Name: DynamoDB
Use Case: Serverless OLTP, gaming, IoT, hyperscale KV
Strengths: Truly serverless, predictable single-digit ms latency, scales to any size
Weaknesses: Costly without single-table design discipline, no joins, query patterns must drive schema
Keywords: dynamodb dax single-table aws nosql kv
Notes: Master single-table design (Alex DeBrie). Use DAX for read-heavy ms→µs caching.

Name: Redis
Use Case: Cache, session, queue, rate limit, leaderboards, pub/sub, streams
Strengths: Sub-ms latency, rich data structures, ubiquitous
Weaknesses: Memory-bound cost, persistence is secondary, cluster has multi-key constraints
Cloud Managed Options: Elasticache, MemoryStore, Azure Cache, Upstash, Redis Cloud
Keywords: redis cache lua streams pubsub sorted set
Notes: Redis 7+ has Functions & RESP3. Use Streams + consumer groups for lightweight queues.

Name: Memcached
Weaknesses: No persistence, no rich types, no replication
Notes: Use only if you literally need a forgettable LRU; Redis is usually a strict superset.

Name: Elasticsearch / OpenSearch
Weaknesses: Operationally heavy, eventual consistency, JVM heap & shard sizing pitfalls
Keywords: elasticsearch opensearch lucene full-text search aggregation
Notes: Plan shard count to dataset size; use ILM for time-series log indices.

Name: ClickHouse
Use Case: Real-time analytics, product analytics, observability backend
Strengths: Insanely fast aggregate queries, columnar compression, materialized views
Weaknesses: Limited UPDATE/DELETE, eventual consistency on replicas
Notes: Pair with Kafka via Kafka engine table for streaming ingestion.

Name: DuckDB
Use Case: Local analytics, ETL, lakehouse query layer
Strengths: Embedded (in-proc), Postgres-like SQL, reads Parquet/Iceberg/Delta directly
Keywords: duckdb embedded olap parquet arrow lakehouse
Notes: Excellent for data-science notebooks, dbt local, lakehouse exploration.

Name: Snowflake / BigQuery / Redshift
Use Case: Enterprise analytics, BI, ML feature store
Strengths: Storage/compute separation, near-zero ops, huge scale
Weaknesses: Cost can run away (especially BigQuery on-demand), latency for small queries
Keywords: snowflake bigquery redshift dwh data warehouse
Notes: Use partition + cluster keys; budget alerts are mandatory.

Name: Neo4j / Memgraph
Use Case: Fraud detection, knowledge graph, recommendations, IAM relationships
Keywords: neo4j cypher graph bolt knowledge graph fraud
Notes: Memgraph is in-memory & API-compatible with much higher throughput.

Name: InfluxDB / TimescaleDB / VictoriaMetrics
Cloud Managed Options: Influx Cloud, Timescale Cloud, Grafana Cloud
Keywords: timeseries tsdb influx timescale victoriametrics metrics
Notes: TimescaleDB lets you keep relational + time-series in one Postgres.

Name: Qdrant / Milvus / Weaviate / pgvector
Use Case: RAG, semantic search, recommendations, embeddings retrieval
Cloud Managed Options: Qdrant Cloud, Zilliz, Weaviate Cloud, Pinecone
Keywords: vector embedding ann hnsw rag semantic search pgvector
Notes: Start with pgvector if Postgres is already your store; move to Qdrant/Milvus when QPS or recall needs grow.

Name: S3 / GCS / Azure Blob
Use Case: Backups, datalakes, static assets, ML datasets
Strengths: Effectively infinite, durable (11×9s), cheap at rest
Weaknesses: Per-request latency, no fine-grained access without IAM design
Keywords: s3 gcs blob object storage data lake
Notes: Use Iceberg/Delta/Hudi to add transactions on top of object storage.

Name: etcd / ZooKeeper / Consul
Use Case: Service discovery, leader election, config, locks
Weaknesses: Not for bulk data, write throughput limited
Keywords: etcd zookeeper consul raft zab leader election service discovery
Notes: Kubernetes uses etcd; ZK is the legacy choice (Kafka pre-KRaft).

Name: SQLite
Use Case: Edge apps, local-first, embedded device, single-tenant SaaS
Weaknesses: Single writer, network access requires wrapper
Keywords: sqlite turso libsql litestream litefs edge
Notes: Modern stacks (Turso, D1, Litestream) make SQLite viable for serverless edge.
